notes.decision: Translated as habitual 'they (habitually) cut them down, since they do not grow' — describing the first class of plants (those without root or seed-bosom) in the kephalaion's botanical typology. The agricultural register matches the seed-and-fruit typology in the lines following.

Greek loanword ζωγραφεῖν 'paint, depict' (cf. ⲍⲱⲣⲁⲫⲉ in glossary). The enthumesis 'paints' the form of the plant where it is located — direct correspondence with cosmological ⲧⲍⲱⲣⲡⲁⲫⲟⲥ 'image-painter' (epithet of Matter). Each plant's enthumesis paints from its own locus (root/branch/fruit).

Translated 'in distress' from ϣⲗⲏ/ϣⲗϩ̄ 'sigh, distress' (Crum). The first class of plants — those that lack root and bosom — have their enthumesis 'placed in distress,' i.e., in a deficient/painful condition lacking proper grounding.

ⲭⲁⲩ = Lyc. ⲕⲱ 'lay down, place'; ⲧⲟⲩⲱ = 'raise' (per terminology guide, must preserve vertical/upward semantics even in agricultural register). The branch-grafting practice: cut a branch, lay it in the soil, and raise it up as a new tree.

Translated 'bosoms' as plural counterpart to ⲕⲟⲩⲟⲩⲛϥ̄ in lines 1-2. The two terms appear to alternate: ⲕⲟⲩⲛϥ̄ for individual seed-bosom, ⲕⲗⲡⲉ̄ for the bosom-cavities of plants that propagate via stem-internal seed/sap. Etymology uncertain — possibly related to ϩⲗⲡⲉ 'navel.'

notes.decision: Chapter title rendered as a unified question across two lines. The dashes — and ϥⲏ markers are decorative section-bracketing devices, not part of the textual content. Title: 'What is the Virgin, or what is he, the Continent?' This frames the dual-term inquiry the disciples raise in lines 15-19.

ⲧⲣⲉⲛ = Lyc. ϯⲣⲉⲛ 'give a name' (in glossary as ϯⲡⲉⲛ). The construction ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲧⲣⲉⲛ ⲁⲣⲁϥ ⲭⲉ X = 'whom they name X.' The disciples are asking why two different titles (παρθένος/ἐγκρατής) are applied to apparently distinct cosmic realities.

ⲡⲓⲥⲉ as 'this matter' is rare; possibly an abbreviation or shortened form of ⲡⲓⲥⲉϫⲉ 'this saying.' Translation follows the standard disciple-petition formula. ⲥⲛⲉⲩ in line 21 = 'two' (Lyc. = Sah. ⲥⲛⲁⲩ), referring to the two terms (virgin/continent) about which they have asked.

The 'virgin' (παρθένος) IS the cosmic title set unto the mystery of the Aeons of the Greatness — i.e., it names the Light that has never descended into the cosmic mingling. The 'continent' (ἐγκρατής), by contrast, names the Light that DID descend, was defiled, and ascended back. The distinction maps onto the Manichaean two-stage Light: Light-as-such (παρθένος) vs. Light-having-suffered-and-returned (ἐγκρατής).

The negated perfect ⲉⲧⲉⲙⲡⲉϥ-ⲭⲓ-ϯⲡⲉ 'which has not taken-taste of death' uses the gustatory register (ϯⲡⲉ = 'taste') common in Manichaean correspondential cosmology. The Virgin-Light has not 'tasted' of death's bitterness — direct sensory-correspondential negation. This formula recurs in line 33 of the new paragraph about holy virgins.

Three-stage descent of the 'continent' Light: came (ⲉⲓ) → was mingled (ⲙⲟⲩⲝⲧ̄) → was defiled (ⲭⲱϩⲙⲉ) — then ascended (ⲃⲱⲕ ⲁϩⲣⲏⲓ̈). This is the classic Manichaean Living Soul trajectory: descent into mingling, suffering in bodies, ascent back to Light. Hence 'continent' = the soul that has exercised continence (ἐγκράτεια) under defilement.

'The holy virgin(s)' opens a new sub-section pivoting from the cosmic-doctrinal exposition (lines 22-31) to a particular class — earthly virgins who go forth against the Enemy. The fragmentary state of lines 31-33 prevents full reconstruction, but the structural parallel (they 'come forth against the Enemy' yet have not 'tasted of death') connects them typologically to the cosmic Virgin-Light of lines 23-26.
